screen.name: Component treatment
screen.purpose: Tell the pay scheme what each component is, so every pay run, payslip and report counts it the right way.

before.name: Formula Engine
before.why: Most answers on this board are worked out from the scheme's formulas.

after.name: Run
after.why: Recompute the pay run so its figures use what you saved.

after.name: Runs
after.why: Each run's card says whether its figures add up.

items.text: Information Technology Jun 2026 — Mid-Cycle Advance was computed before your last change to this scheme. Recompute it so its figures use the change.

fields.if_changed: Read-only here. Change where a value comes from in Mapping › Connections.
fields.filled_by: Read from where the value arrives: a formula on this scheme, a connected system, the month's spreadsheet, the contract or a fixed value. The small grey chips beside it are values that actually arrived.

fields.if_changed: Only how components are grouped on screens and reports changes; no amount changes. Payslips already computed keep the old group until you recompute the run.
fields.label: Component Type
fields.help: The report group: organises the grid and reports, such as Earnings or Deductions. Filled from the pay role; a group a person types is kept. The spreadsheet's own section heading is kept separately.
fields.filled_by: Filled from the pay role: Earnings, Deductions, Net pay, Employer costs or Information. Type a group of your own and it is kept; clear the box to go back to the automatic one.

fields.if_changed: Reports use the new role from now on. Payslips already computed keep the old role until you recompute the run.
fields.label: Net Pay Role
fields.help: What the net pay formula does with this component. Derived from the scheme's own formulas, not from the component's name.

choices.label: Added to net pay
choices.when: Pay the person receives: salary, allowances, overtime pay.

choices.label: Taken off net pay
choices.when: Money taken from the person's pay: their insurance share, tax, a loan repayment.

choices.label: Net pay itself
choices.when: The final take-home figure. One component per scheme.

choices.label: Employer cost
choices.when: Paid by the company on top of pay, such as the employer's insurance share. It never reaches the person.

choices.label: Information only
choices.when: Shown, never counted: hours, days, rates, codes and dates.

choices.label: Both added and taken off
choices.when: The formulas both add it and take it off. It usually needs splitting into two components.

fields.filled_by: Worked out from the scheme's own formulas when you press Re-classify from the formulas. A role you choose is marked Set by a person and is kept on every re-classify. Only an amount can be added to or taken off net pay.

fields.if_changed: Totals start or stop counting this line, so the same money is never counted twice. The line still shows on the payslip. Recompute the run to update payslips already computed.
fields.label: Folded Into a Total
fields.help: This component is already included in another component of the same kind, so a pay run counts the total and not this line. The line still shows on the payslip.
fields.filled_by: Ticked from the formulas when this amount is already counted inside another component, such as an allowance inside gross pay. Re-classify keeps a tick you changed yourself.

fields.if_changed: The next pay run reads the new signal, and it can change who gets a payslip. Check the number of people in the run after you change it.
fields.label: Run signal
fields.help: Some components say something about the PERSON rather than about their pay, and the run has to act on them — whether to produce a payslip at all, for instance.

choices.label: Whether the person is still employed
choices.when: The pay run reads it to decide whether a person still gets a payslip.

choices.label: Hours actually worked
choices.when: The pay run reads it as the hours each person actually worked.

fields.filled_by: Suggested during setup from the component's name and sample values; you choose it here. Leave it blank for an ordinary pay component.

fields.if_changed: New values are read the new way. Values already stored on payslips stay as they were until you recompute the run. Choosing a type that is not an amount sets its pay role to Information only.
fields.label: Value type
fields.help: What this component's value IS. Decides whether it is stored as a number or kept exactly as it arrived, whether it can become a payslip line, and how it is displayed. The first five are numbers; the last four are not and are never converted.

choices.label: Amount (currency)
choices.when: An amount of money. The only type that can be added to or taken off net pay.

choices.label: Quantity (hours, days)
choices.when: Hours or days. Its pay role can only be Information only; the pay comes from the formula that multiplies it.

choices.label: Text
choices.when: Words kept exactly as they arrive, such as a location a formula compares against.

fields.filled_by: Worked out when the scheme is imported, from the spreadsheet's values, its date and percentage formats and the formulas. New pay data can refine it when you re-classify. A type you choose is never overwritten.

actions.label: Re-classify from the formulas
actions.effect: Works out value types, pay roles, totals and report groups again. Choices you saved are kept.

actions.label: Set all of them to Information only
actions.effect: Every row whose value type says otherwise becomes Information only, marked as set by you.

actions.label: Save
actions.effect: Saves the rows you changed. Payslips keep their values until you recompute the run.

tasks.name: Fix figures that do not add up

terms.definition: What a scheme does with each component: its pay role, whether it is already included in another total, and its value type. It belongs to the scheme, so it affects every run.
What net pay does with a component: adds it, takes it off, is it, counts it as employer cost, or ignores it. Every gross, deductions and net figure is counted from it.
A line whose parts are already counted elsewhere, like gross income. Ticking it stops the totals counting the same money twice.
What a value is: an amount, a quantity such as hours or days, a percentage, text, a date or yes/no. Only an amount can be added to or taken off net pay.
